bib.title: GPipe: Easy Scaling with Micro-Batch Pipeline Parallelism

read.skipped: Supplementary material (training configs, code examples) is referenced but not in the PDF.

question: Can a task-independent pipeline-parallelism library let any network expressible as a sequence of layers scale past one accelerator's memory with near-linear speedup?
hypothesis: Splitting mini-batches into micro-batches and pipelining them with re-materialization and synchronous gradient accumulation gives efficient, consistent model parallelism; larger models give better quality.
contributions: GPipe library with a batch-splitting pipeline-parallelism algorithm and synchronous gradient updates
Scaling a 557M AmoebaNet to 84.4% top-1 ImageNet
A single 6B-parameter 128-layer multilingual Transformer beating bilingual baselines on 100 language pairs

method.summary: Layers are partitioned into K cells on K accelerators; each mini-batch of N is split into M micro-batches pipelined through the cells, gradients accumulated and applied synchronously, with re-materialization at partition boundaries. Evaluated on throughput/max model size (AmoebaNet, Transformer), ImageNet/transfer image classification, and 103-language NMT.

limits: GPipe assumes a single layer fits in one accelerator's memory (footnote 3 offers splitting a matmul across layers).
Imperfect partitioning gives load imbalance; AmoebaNet scaled sub-linearly (1.8B on 8 accelerators, 25x not 8x-linear) and its throughput speedup is sub-linear.
BatchNorm needs special handling (micro-batch statistics in training, mini-batch moving average in evaluation).
Deep NMT models had trainability issues (peaky predictions, non-finite gradients); fixed with scaled init and logit clipping, threshold value not given.

Throughput numbers are single measurements without variance; NMT results are shown in a figure with no table; NMT corpus is in-house; training steps, learning rates and compute are in supplementary material, not in this PDF.
Table 2 normalization baseline is not spelled out in the text.
Table 1 max-size results depend on 12 bytes/parameter with RMSProp.
